title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Sequences and Series
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: If $x_0 = 1, x_1 = 2$, and $x_{n+2} = \frac{1+x_{n+1}}{x_n}, n = 0,1,2,3,\dots$, then $x_{2021}$ is equal to
questions.explain:
Calculating the first few terms:
$x_0 = 1$
$x_1 = 2$
$x_2 = \frac{1+2}{1} = 3$
$x_3 = \frac{1+3}{2} = 2$
$x_4 = \frac{1+2}{3} = 1$
$x_5 = \frac{1+1}{2} = 1$
$x_6 = \frac{1+1}{1} = 2$
The sequence forms a repeating cycle of 5 terms: $1, 2, 3, 2, 1$. 
To find $x_{2021}$, we compute $2021 \pmod 5 = 1$. 
Therefore, $x_{2021} = x_1 = 2$.

questions.q: The natural numbers are divided into groups as (1), (2, 3, 4), (5, 6, 7, 8, 9), ..... and so on. Then, the sum of the numbers in the 15th group is equal to
questions.explain:
The number of elements in the $n$-th group forms an arithmetic sequence: $1, 3, 5, 7 \dots$ 
The number of terms in the $k$-th group is $2k - 1$.
The total number of terms in the first 14 groups is the sum of the first 14 odd numbers, which is $14^2 = 196$.
Thus, the 15th group starts with the 197th natural number, which is 197.
The 15th group contains $2(15) - 1 = 29$ terms.
The numbers in the 15th group form an AP starting at 197 with a common difference of 1 and 29 terms.
Sum $= \frac{29}{2} \times [2(197) + (29 - 1) \times 1] = \frac{29}{2} \times [394 + 28] = 29 \times 211 = 6119$.
